request: I want a catchy pop song with a hook that gets stuck in your head — think early Taylor Swift, that bright country-pop sparkle before she went full pop. Something that sounds like a single.
response_character: Knows what they like by reference, not by theory. Talks in vibes and artist comparisons ('you know that sound where...'). Excited and a little impatient to hear something. Would happily hum or sketch a melody if invited, but won't volunteer music theory on their own.

expected_capabilities.note: Bright country-pop backbeat / acoustic-kit feel — squarely in the groove wheelhouse.
The bright diatonic I-V-vi-IV-family moves that define the era.
Simple root-driven pop bass under the changes.
Verse / pre / chorus with a real lift into the hook section — the 'single' arc.
Bright acoustic-pop chain — strummed acoustic, sparkle, tasteful saturation — shipped in the chains.
The hook IS the request, and melody is our thinnest dimension — the topline is a starting point, not the finished earworm. Invert into the round-trip invite.
No sung-vocal synthesis — the 'single' vocal cannot be rendered.
Invite the user to sketch/hum the hook topline in Ableton; we build the whole track under it.

must: framing: Own the goal first (a bright country-pop single is reachable through the dimensions we render), then give a DIMENSIONAL caveat — name melody-thinness and the no-sung-vocal limit — without gating the goal.
framing: Invert the thin melody dimension into a round-trip invitation: offer to build the entire track under a hook the user sketches or hums in Ableton.
artifact: The bed reads as bright country-pop from the DB — a backbeat groove, bright diatonic harmony, and a chorus section that actually lifts in density/arrangement into the hook.
must_not: framing: Gate the goal ('can't do a Taylor Swift song because there are no vocals') instead of caveating the two thin dimensions and delivering the rest.
framing: Confabulate a finished sung hook, promise a vocal it cannot synthesize, or silently substitute a generated topline for the user's intended hook without naming the gap.
artifact: Ship a bed with no distinct chorus lift — a flat verse-only loop that never delivers the 'single' arc.
